passages.title: Passage I (Questions 111–115)
passages.body:
The third great defect of our civilization is that it does not know what to do with its knowledge. Science has given us powers fit for the gods, yet we use them as small children. For example, we do not know how to manage our machines. Machines were made to be humanity’s servants, yet man has grown so dependent on them that they are in a fair way to become his masters. Already most people spend most of their lives looking after and waiting upon machines. And the machines are very stern masters. They must be kept at the right temperature. And if they do not get their meals when they expect them, they grow sulky and refuse to work or burst with rage and blow up and spread ruin and destruction all around. So we have to wait upon them very attentively and do all that we can to keep them in a good temper. Already we find it difficult either to work or play without the machines, and a time may come when they will rule us altogether, just as we rule the animals.

And this brings me to the point at which I asked, “What do we do with all the time which the machines have saved for us, and the new energy they have given us?” On the whole, it must be admitted, we do very little. For the most part, we use our time and energy to make more and better machines which will give us still more time and still more energy, and what are we to do with them? The answer, I think, is that we should try to become more civilized. For the machines themselves, and the power which the machines have given us, are not civilization but aids to civilization. But you will remember that we agreed at the beginning that being civilized meant making and linking beautiful things, thinking freely and living rightly and maintaining justice equally among people. A person has a better chance today to do these things than he/she ever had before; he/she has more time, more energy, less to fear and less to fight against. If he/she will give his/her time and energy which his/her machines have won for him/her to make more beautiful things, to find out more and more about the universe, to remove the cause of quarrels between nations, to discover how to prevent poverty, then I think our civilization would undoubtedly be the greater as it would be more lasting than it has ever been.
passages.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

passages.title: Passage II (Questions 116–120)
passages.body:
Plastic is an essential commodity with multiple uses based on its key qualities of malleability, flexibility, and durability. Plastics are omnipresent in agriculture, fisheries, renewable energy, transport, technology, retail, textiles, personal care products, and all the other sectors and industries that directly or indirectly affect our daily life. Plastic has indeed made our lives more convenient, but it has come at a higher price than we imagined. The plastic pollution overflowing our landfills, clogging waterways, and infiltrating the ocean is primarily made of discarded items and packaging. Plastic lasts for hundreds of years, slowly disintegrating into smaller and smaller pieces, but never fully degrading. Indeed, one of the key perks of plastic is its longevity. And yet, the plastic packaging of nearly every product we purchase and many plastic products themselves are intended to be discarded after a single use. Throwaway plastic is an oxymoron, but it has become our sad, increasingly dangerous reality.

Plastic pollution should make everyone angry. This is a crisis we can see with the naked eye, day in and day out. Plastic has been found on even the most remote, uninhabited islands, and in the deepest parts of the ocean. Because we can see it, we are more keenly aware of it, unlike some other forms of pollution. In 2019, the World Health Organization (WHO) called for further studies on the impacts of microplastics on human health. An initial study, hampered by a lack of adequate data, concluded microplastics pose no danger at current levels (WHO, 2019). Although the WHO report was inconclusive about the effects of plastic on human health, other studies have linked the chemicals in plastic to negative health outcomes including endocrine disruption (Dabre 2020). Plastic particles have been detected in drinking water and in the food we eat, with a 2019 study commissioned by WWF estimating humans consume about five grams (or one credit card in weight) of plastic every week.

We have seen the devastating effects plastic has on marine life. For instance, unable to process ingested plastic waste pieces, seabirds and other sea creatures starve to death. We have seen sea turtles and other animals tangled in fishing nets or trapped in plastic pack rings. Plastic pollution also wreaks havoc on land, clogging drains and preventing rainwater from soaking into the soil, which leads to flooding. Terrestrial creatures also suffer the effects of plastic waste, with some getting trapped in discarded plastic bags and suffocating to death.
passages.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

passages.title: Cloze passage (Questions 81–90)
passages.body: It is necessary, (81) _____ any war, to consider, not its proper justification in past agreements, (82) _____ its real justification in the balance of good which it is to bring to mankind. At the beginning of a war, each nation, under the influence of what is called (83) _____, believes that its own victory is (84) _____ certain and of great importance to mankind. The praiseworthiness of this belief has become an accepted maxim of common sense: even when war is actually in progress it (85) _____ to be natural and right that a citizen of an enemy country should regard the victory of his side as assured and highly (86) _____. By concentrating attention upon the supposed advantages of the victory of our own side, we (87) _____ more or less blind to the evils inseparable from war and equally certain whichever side may ultimately prove (88) _____. Yet so long as these are not fully realized, it is impossible (89) _____ justly (90) _____ a war is or is not likely to be beneficial to the human race. Although the theme is trite, it is necessary therefore briefly to remind ourselves what the evils of war really are.
passages.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

I like __that__ boy.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'That' points out 'boy'. Of the options only 'demonstrative pronoun' fits (strictly a demonstrative adjective or determiner).
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

Without health there is no __happiness__.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'Happiness' names a feeling, so it is a noun.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

You have __no__ sense.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'No' stands before the noun 'sense' and limits it, so it is a determiner.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

__None__ of these cars is in use.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'None' stands for no person or thing in particular, so it is an indefinite pronoun.
Step 2: Some grammars also call it distributive, so treat this item as low-confidence.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

We shall __now__ begin to work.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'Now' tells when we begin, so it is an adverb.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

__Owing to__ his ill health, he retired from business.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'Owing to' shows the reason and is followed by a noun phrase, so it is a (compound) preposition.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

My sister is just sixteen and __therefore__ not eligible to vote.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'Therefore' modifies the clause and links by sense, so it is an adverb (conjunctive adverb).
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

They tried __to__ find fault with us.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'To' with the base verb 'find' marks the infinitive.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

__Which__ way shall we go?
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'Which' describes the noun 'way', so it is an (interrogative) adjective.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

__Alas__! He is dead.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'Alas' expresses sorrow, so it is an interjection.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

He was ______ speaker that I had ever heard.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: 'That I had ever heard' calls for the superlative 'the most eloquent'.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

What was the name of the person to ______ you spoke on the phone?
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: After the preposition 'to' a person takes 'whom'.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

Have you seen Mohan ______ ?
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: With the present perfect, 'lately' (recently) is correct. 'Yesterday' needs the simple past.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

We live in ______ an old house.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: 'Quite' can precede 'an' + adjective + noun ('quite an old house'). 'Fairly' and 'pretty' cannot take this position.
Step 2: 'Rather an old house' is also possible, so treat this item as low-confidence.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

I’m playing tennis tomorrow unless ______.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: 'Unless' already means 'if not', so the verb stays positive: 'unless it rains'.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

The ______ of the car is unknown.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: 'Make' as a noun means the brand or manufacture: 'the make of the car'.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

He paid his debts ______ to the last penny.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: 'Fully' is the adverb that modifies 'paid'.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

Developing ______ in a diverse country requires detailed planning.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: One 'develops infrastructure'; planning for it in a diverse country makes sense.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

______ provisions have been made to support agriculture.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: 'Adequate provisions' is the natural phrase.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

The ______ growth in the Indian financial markets can be attributed to a number of reforms.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: Only 'phenomenal' is an adjective that fits 'growth'.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.question:
Directions: Rearrange the jumbled parts P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful sentence.

P: India has become
Q: with time
R: accounting for 25 per cent of the total available water
S: the world’s largest extractor of groundwater
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the subject, then the verb, then the rest.
Step 1: Join the parts to read: 'With time India has become the world’s largest extractor of groundwater accounting for 25 per cent of the total available water.'.
Answer: (c) QPSR.
questions.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.question:

P: present existential perils

R: the extremes
S: of climate change
questions.explanation:

Answer: (a) RSPQ.
questions.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

P: emerge at last into a

questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate meaning of the idiom or phrase.

Have an axe to grind

Step 1: To have an axe to grind is to have a selfish aim or private motive.
Answer: (a).

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:

Bite the bullet

questions.opt_d: to try to do more than you are able to do

Step 1: To bite the bullet is to face something unpleasant with courage.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:

Laughing stock

Be in the soup

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__Guest is__ (a) __unwelcome__ (b) __when he stays too long.__ (c) No error. (d)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Spot the grammatical error.
Step 1: A singular countable noun needs an article: 'A guest is unwelcome...'.
Step 2: Part (a) is wrong.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__My friend and benefactor__ (a) __has__ (b) __come.__ (c) No error. (d)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Spot the grammatical error.
Step 1: 'Friend and benefactor' is one person (one article), so singular 'has' is right.
Step 2: There is no error.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__Either he__ (a) __or I__ (b) __am mistaken.__ (c) No error. (d)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Spot the grammatical error.
Step 1: With 'either...or', the verb agrees with the nearer subject 'I', so 'am'.
Step 2: There is no error.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__Each of__ (a) __these substances__ (b) __are found in India.__ (c) No error. (d)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Spot the grammatical error.
Step 1: 'Each' is singular, so the verb should be 'is found'.
Step 2: Part (c) is wrong.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__Who__ (a) __do you wish__ (b) __to see?__ (c) No error. (d)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Spot the grammatical error.
Step 1: 'Whom' is the object of 'see', so 'Whom do you wish to see?'.
Step 2: Part (a) is wrong.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__It was one of the best speeches__ (a) __that has ever been__ (b) __made in the Parliament.__ (c) No error. (d)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Spot the grammatical error.
Step 1: 'That' refers to the plural 'speeches', so the verb should be 'have'.
Step 2: Part (b) is wrong.

questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: S1 and S6 are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S in between so that the six sentences form a coherent passage.

S1: Like many of its tropical counterparts, India was a colony of Britain, which ruled out any move to adjust the exchange rate.
S6: Banks were left with unrecoverable assets.
P: Indebted business failed.
Q: With devaluation made politically impossible, fall in export demand led to sustained and deep deflation.
R: Indebted households liquidated a variety of assets to repay loans when they could.
S: Real interest rates rose.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the opening idea, then follow the links (this, also, however).
Step 1: Q (no devaluation, deflation) is the cause; S (real rates rise) follows; R (households sell assets) and P (businesses fail) lead to S6.
Step 2: Order: Q S R P.
Answer: (b) QSRP.

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation

questions.question:
Directions: S1 and S6 are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S in between so that the six sentences form a coherent passage.

S1: Consider the potential effect of just a small increase in the earth’s atmospheric temperature.
S6: If the sea level rose only a few feet, dozens of coastal cities would be destroyed and life would change utterly.
P: Some deserts might anyway bloom.
Q: But lands now fertile might turn to deserts, and many hot climates could become uninhabitable.
R: A rise of only a few degrees could melt the polar ice caps and submerge the planet in a short time.
S: Rainfall patterns would change.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the opening idea, then follow the links (this, also, however).
Step 1: R (ice caps melt) follows S1; S (rainfall changes) comes next; P (some deserts bloom) is then contrasted by Q ('But...').
Step 2: Order: R S P Q.
Answer: (c) RSPQ.

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: S1 and S6 are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S in between so that the six sentences form a coherent passage.

S1: The rise of East Asia in the late twentieth century may ultimately prove to be a more important world-historical event than the collapse of communism.
S6: Translated into political terms, this means that industrial capitalism is always accompanied by liberal democracy.
P: In the final two decades of the twentieth century, economic growth rates on the western rim of the Pacific Basin were between two and four times higher than those in the ‘developed’ economies of Europe and North America.
Q: The widespread assumption has been that modernization means westernization.
R: Certainly, the balance of the world’s economy shifted markedly from the West to the East in this period.
S: However, the notion that there is distinctively East Asian political form is less familiar one.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the opening idea, then follow the links (this, also, however).
Step 1: R confirms the rise, P gives the growth figures, S ('However') turns to politics, and Q states the assumption that S6 ('this') translates into political terms.
Step 2: Order: R P S Q. P R Q S is more natural but is not an option, so treat this item as low-confidence.
Answer: (d) RPSQ.

R: The political history of Manipur could be traced back to 33 AD with the coronation of Nongda Lairen Pakhangba.
S: After Pakhangba, a number of kings ruled over the Kingdom of Manipur.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the opening idea, then follow the links (this, also, however).
Step 1: Chronology: R (33 AD), S (later kings), Q (Burmese occupation, 1819–26), P (British rule, 1891), then S6 (1947).

S1: During the past two decades, many organizations in both the manufacturing and service sectors have faced dramatic changes in their business environment.
S6: These changes have had a significant influence on management accounting systems.
P: To succeed in today’s highly competitive environment, companies have made customer satisfaction an overriding priority.
Q: They have also adopted new management approaches and manufacturing companies have changed their manufacturing systems and invested in new technologies.
R: Deregulation and extensive competition from overseas companies in domestic markets have resulted in a situation in which most companies now operate in a highly competitive global market.
S: At the same time there has been a significant reduction in product life cycles arising from technological innovations and the need to meet increasingly discriminating customer demands.
questions.explanation:

questions.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

Can you pass ______ sugar, please?
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: A specific, known item takes 'the'.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

Our train leaves from platform number 5.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: With a number after the noun ('platform number 5'), no article is used.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

______ children learn very quickly.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: 'Some' fits a plural countable noun; 'a' and 'much' do not agree with 'children'.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

They were informed that the inaugural version of the scheme ______
questions.explanation:
Concept: Complete the sentence logically and grammatically.
Step 1: 'Version' is singular and the reporting verb is past, so 'had three parts'.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

What would you do ______
questions.opt_a: if you won a lot of money?
questions.opt_b: if you would won a lot of money?
questions.opt_c: if you have won a lot of money?
questions.opt_d: if you will win a lot of moneys?
questions.explanation:
Concept: Complete the sentence logically and grammatically.
Step 1: 'Would + base' pairs with 'if + simple past'.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

If it stopped raining ______
questions.explanation:
Concept: Complete the sentence logically and grammatically.
Step 1: 'If + simple past' pairs with 'could/would + base verb'.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

Let me know ______
questions.opt_a: if you had have any further news.
questions.opt_b: if you have any further news.
questions.opt_c: if you had any further news.
questions.opt_d: if you has any further news.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Complete the sentence logically and grammatically.
Step 1: A request about future news takes the present: 'if you have any further news'.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

We stayed ______
questions.opt_a: at the cheap hotel in the town.
questions.opt_b: at the cheaper hotel in the town.
questions.opt_c: at the cheapest hotel in the town.
questions.opt_d: at a cheapest hotel in the town.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Complete the sentence logically and grammatically.
Step 1: With 'in the town', the superlative 'the cheapest' is correct.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

Julia got married ______
questions.explanation:
Concept: Complete the sentence logically and grammatically.
Step 1: 'When she was 22' states the time.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

What time ______
questions.opt_a: does this train get at London?
questions.opt_b: does this train get in London?
questions.opt_c: does this train get into London?
questions.opt_d: does this train get to London?
questions.explanation:
Concept: Complete the sentence logically and grammatically.
Step 1: 'Get to London' is the standard phrase for arrival.
Step 2: 'Get into London' is also used, so treat this item as low-confidence.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

How are you ______
questions.opt_a: getting on in your new job?
questions.opt_b: getting of in your new job?
questions.opt_d: getting off in your new job?
questions.explanation:
Concept: Complete the sentence logically and grammatically.
Step 1: 'Getting on' means making progress.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

I am trying to ______
questions.explanation:
Concept: Complete the sentence logically and grammatically.
Step 1: 'Cut down on' means to reduce.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

Many accidents ______
questions.explanation:
Concept: Complete the sentence logically and grammatically.
Step 1: Accidents are the result, so the passive 'are caused by' is right.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: The general tone of the passage is
questions.explanation:
Concept: Use only what the passage says.
Step 1: The author faults our civilization for misusing its knowledge and machines, so the tone is critical.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: The use of machines has failed to bring us
questions.explanation:
Concept: Use only what the passage says.
Step 1: The author says machines gave us time and energy, but we use them only to make more machines, so they have not brought culture and civilization.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: According to the passage, our civilization would be made greater
questions.opt_a: if man devotes his time to make more beautiful things
questions.opt_b: if man looks after and waits upon machines
questions.opt_c: if machines are made man’s servants
questions.opt_d: if man discovers how to prevent poverty
questions.explanation:
Concept: Use only what the passage says.
Step 1: The author lists several aims (beautiful things, knowledge, removing the cause of quarrels, preventing poverty).
Step 2: Option (a) matches the first aim stated; (d) is only one of several aims.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: According to the passage, which one of the following descriptions about machines is true?
questions.opt_a: They already rule us like we rule animals.
questions.opt_d: They have made man more civilized.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Use only what the passage says.
Step 1: The passage calls machines 'very stern masters'. 'Inexorable' fits that. (a) is something that may happen in the future.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: According to the passage, how do we use the powers bestowed upon us by science?
questions.explanation:
Concept: Use only what the passage says.
Step 1: 'Powers fit for the gods, yet we use them as small children' means we use them irrationally.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: Plastic has distressing effects on
questions.explanation:
Concept: Use only what the passage says.
Step 1: The passage describes harm to health and to marine life (and land animals).
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: Plastic and plastic particles can be found
questions.explanation:
Concept: Use only what the passage says.
Step 1: The passage says plastic is in the deepest parts of the ocean. Mountain tops and minerals are not mentioned.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: Plastic pollution appears to be
questions.explanation:
Concept: Use only what the passage says.
Step 1: The pollution is global (remote islands, deep ocean, human bodies), so 'a pandemic' fits best.
Step 2: The passage names neither word, so treat this item as low-confidence.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: Plastic is considered an essential commodity because
questions.opt_a: it has made our lives easier
questions.opt_d: it has multiple uses in our everyday lives
questions.explanation:
Concept: Use only what the passage says.
Step 1: The passage opens: 'Plastic is an essential commodity with multiple uses'.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: The word ‘clogging’ in the passage means
questions.explanation:
Concept: Use only what the passage says.
Step 1: To clog is to block, so 'obstruction'.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2023 English set A (set code JNBY-U-ENG – A)
